models.name: discussion_board_admin_requests
models.description:
Administrator application requests submitted by members seeking privilege escalation. Each request includes justification reason, current status (pending/approved/rejected), and submission timestamp. Super administrators review and decide on requests, with decision recorded for audit trail.

Key relationships:
- {@link discussion_board_members}: The member who submitted the request
- {@link discussion_board_admins}: The super administrator who made the decision (nullable until decided)
- {@link discussion_board_admin_request_histories}: Audit trail of all status transitions

Business constraints:
- Single pending request per member (enforced by unique index on member_id with status filter at application layer)
- Status transitions: pending → approved/rejected (immutable after decision)
- Reason text required (50-2000 characters per validation rules)

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: The member who submitted the administrator application request. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: The super administrator who reviewed and decided on this request. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Justification text explaining why the member requests administrator privileges. Required field with 50-2000 character validation.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current request status: pending (awaiting review), approved (promoted to administrator), or rejected (denied). Transitions from pending to approved/rejected are immutable.

plainFields.name: submitted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member submitted the administrator request. Used for sorting pending queue and enforcing waiting periods.

plainFields.name: decided_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the super administrator made the decision (approved/rejected). Null while status is pending.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp for audit trail.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp for change tracking.

models.name: discussion_board_admin_request_histories
models.description:
Audit trail recording all status transitions of administrator application requests. Each history entry captures when a request's status changed, which super administrator made the decision, and the reason for rejection if applicable. This table provides complete audit compliance for privilege escalation workflows and administrative transparency.

Related entities: {@link discussion_board_admin_requests} (parent request being audited), {@link discussion_board_admins} (super administrator who made the decision).

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_admin_request_id
foreignFields.description: Parent admin request's {@link discussion_board_admin_requests.id} being audited.

foreignFields.name: deciding_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Super administrator's {@link discussion_board_admins.id} who made the status decision.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Request status at this transition point. Values: pending, approved, rejected.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Optional reason text for rejection decisions. Null for approvals or pending status.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this status transition occurred.

models.name: discussion_board_bans
models.description:
Active ban records that restrict user access to the platform.

Stores current bans imposed by administrators on members, including the ban reason and timestamp. Each banned user has exactly one active ban record at any time. When a user is unbanned, the record is soft-deleted and an entry is added to the ban history audit trail.

Banned users cannot log in but their existing articles and comments remain visible per content preservation policy. Administrators can view the banned users list with ban reasons for transparency.

Related entities: {@link discussion_board_members} (banned user), {@link discussion_board_admins} (enforcing administrator), {@link discussion_board_ban_histories} (audit trail).

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: Banned member's {@link discussion_board_members.id}. The user whose access is restricted by this ban.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Enforcing administrator's {@link discussion_board_admins.id}. The administrator who imposed this ban.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Ban reason explaining why the user was banned. Required for administrative transparency and must meet minimum/maximum length validation requirements.

plainFields.name: banned_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the ban was imposed. Automatically recorded at ban creation and immutable thereafter for audit integrity.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Set when user is unbanned to preserve audit history while marking ban as inactive.

models.name: discussion_board_ban_histories
models.description:
Audit trail of all ban and unban events with timestamps and action-specific reasons.

This table maintains a complete history of all ban-related actions for compliance and transparency. Each record captures either a ban or unban event, including the action type and reason provided by the administrator at the time of the action.

Related to {@link discussion_board_bans} for the parent ban record (which contains member and administrator references), {@link discussion_board_members} for the affected user account (via ban relationship), and {@link discussion_board_admins} for the administrator who performed the action (via ban relationship).

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_ban_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent ban record. {@link discussion_board_bans.id}. Member and administrator references are accessible through this relationship.

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: Type of action performed: 'banned' or 'unbanned'. Distinguishes between ban imposition and ban removal events.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Action-specific reason provided by the administrator. Required for ban events, optional for unban events. Captures the context for this specific history entry.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the ban or unban action was recorded. Immutable after creation for audit integrity.

### `discussion_board_guests`

Guest accounts for unauthenticated visitors identified by device
fingerprint for temporary session tracking.

Guests represent anonymous users who browse the discussion board without
traditional authentication. Each guest is identified by a unique device
fingerprint, enabling temporary session management and basic tracking
without requiring email/password credentials. Guests have read-only
access to sections, articles, and comments but cannot create content or
manage profiles.

Related to [discussion_board_guest_sessions](#discussion_board_guest_sessions) through one-to-many
relationship where each guest can have multiple sessions over time.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `device_fingerprint`
  > Unique device fingerprint identifier for guest tracking. Generated from
  > browser/device characteristics to distinguish anonymous visitors without
  > requiring authentication.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the guest record was first created. Used for tracking
  > guest lifecycle and session management.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the guest record was last updated. Updated on each session
  > activity for tracking purposes.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the guest record was soft deleted. Null for active
  > records. Enables data retention and audit trail while removing guest from
  > active queries.

### `discussion_board_guest_sessions`

Temporary session tokens for guest users with expiration for anonymous
browsing access.

Tracks guest user sessions for stateless authentication during anonymous
browsing. Each session represents a single browsing session with
connection metadata and expiration time for automatic cleanup. Sessions
are created when guests access the platform and expire after the
configured duration.

Related to [discussion_board_guests](#discussion_board_guests) through many-to-one
relationship (multiple sessions per guest).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_guest_id`: Belonged guest's [discussion_board_guests.id](#discussion_board_guests).
- `ip`: Client IP address for session tracking and security audit.
- `href`: Initial page URL where the session was created.
- `referrer`: HTTP referrer header indicating traffic source.
- `created_at`: Session creation timestamp.
- `expired_at`: Session expiration timestamp for automatic invalidation.

### `discussion_board_members`

Registered member accounts with email and password authentication. Stores
profile information including display name shown publicly and biography
text. Tracks account status for lifecycle management including active,
suspended, and deleted states. Members can create articles, post
comments, and request administrator status.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Email address for authentication and account identification. Must be
  > unique across all member accounts.
- `password_hash`
  > Hashed password credential for authentication. Never stores plain text
  > passwords.
- `display_name`
  > Public display name shown on articles, comments, and profile pages.
  > Visible to all users including guests.
- `bio`
  > Biography text for member profile. Optional personal description visible
  > on profile page.
- `status`
  > Account status for lifecycle management. Values: active, suspended,
  > deleted. Controls login ability and content visibility.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the member account was created. Immutable after initial
  > registration.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the member account was last updated. Updated on every
  > profile or credential change.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the member account was soft deleted. Null for active
  > accounts. Enables account deletion cascade.

### `discussion_board_member_sessions`

JWT session tokens for member authentication with access and refresh
token support.

Stores active and expired session records for registered members. Each
session represents a distinct login event with connection metadata for
security auditing. Sessions are managed through authentication flows and
serve as an append-only audit trail of member login activity.

Related to [discussion_board_members](#discussion_board_members) through many-to-one
relationship. Multiple sessions can exist per member for concurrent
device access.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_member_id`: Belonged member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members).
- `ip`: IP address of the client device at session creation.
- `href`: URL of the page where authentication was initiated.
- `referrer`: HTTP referrer header value at session creation.
- `created_at`: Session creation timestamp.
- `expired_at`: Session expiration timestamp for automatic invalidation.

### `discussion_board_member_password_resets`

Password reset tokens for member password recovery workflow. Stores
temporary tokens with expiration timestamps that members use to reset
their forgotten passwords. Each token is single-use and becomes invalid
after expiration or use.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_member_id`: Belonged member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members).
- `token`: Unique password reset token sent to member's email for verification.
- `expires_at`: Expiration timestamp when the reset token becomes invalid.
- `used_at`: Timestamp when the reset token was used, null if not yet used.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the password reset request was created.

### `discussion_board_member_email_verifications`

Email verification tokens for member registration and email confirmation
process. Stores one-time verification tokens with expiration to validate
email addresses during account creation and email changes. Each token is
unique and can only be used once before expiration.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_member_id`: Belonged member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members).
- `email`
  > Email address being verified. Stored for validation even if member email
  > changes during verification process.
- `token`
  > Unique verification token sent to the email address. Used for one-time
  > email confirmation.
- `expires_at`
  > Token expiration timestamp. Verification fails after this time to prevent
  > stale token usage.
- `verified_at`
  > Timestamp when the email was successfully verified. Null if not yet
  > verified or expired.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.

### `discussion_board_admins`

Administrator accounts with elevated privileges for platform governance
and content moderation. Administrators are promoted from regular members
through an approval process and have two grade levels: regular
administrators can manage sections, delete content, and ban users; super
administrators have additional powers to approve admin requests and
manage other administrators' grades. Each admin record maintains a 1:1
relationship with a member account, preserving the member's original
identity while granting elevated permissions.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `member_id`
  > Belonged member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members). Administrator
  > accounts are promoted from existing members, maintaining a 1:1
  > relationship with the original member account.
- `grade`
  > Administrator grade level determining privilege scope. 'regular'
  > administrators can manage sections, delete content, and ban users.
  > 'super' administrators have elevated powers including approving admin
  > requests and managing other administrators' grades.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the administrator account was created (when the admin
  > request was approved).
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the administrator record was last updated, such as grade
  > changes.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the administrator privileges were revoked (soft delete).
  > Null means active administrator.

### `discussion_board_admin_sessions`

JWT session tokens for administrator authentication with enhanced
security. Tracks login sessions including connection metadata (IP
address, referrer, href) and temporal fields for audit compliance.
Sessions are append-only records managed through the authentication flow,
providing an audit trail of all administrator access events.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_admin_id`
  > Belonged administrator's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins). Establishes
  > the session's association with the administrator account.
- `ip`
  > IP address of the administrator's connection at session creation. Used
  > for security monitoring and audit trail.
- `href`
  > URL of the page where the administrator initiated the login. Provides
  > context for the authentication event.
- `referrer`
  > HTTP referrer header from the login request. Tracks the navigation path
  > leading to authentication.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the session was created. Marks the beginning of the
  > session's validity period.
- `expired_at`
  > Timestamp when the session expires. Sessions are invalid after this time
  > and must be refreshed or re-authenticated.

### `discussion_board_admin_audit_logs`

Audit trail logging all administrator actions including bans, content
deletion, section management, and admin request decisions. Provides
compliance tracking and administrative transparency for all elevated
privilege operations.

Each record captures a single administrative action with the acting
administrator, action type, target entity, and contextual details. This
table is append-only and serves as the authoritative audit log for
regulatory compliance and security investigations.

Related to [discussion_board_admins](#discussion_board_admins) through the admin foreign key
relationship.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `admin_id`
  > Acting administrator's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins) who performed
  > the audited action.
- `action_type`
  > Type of administrative action performed. Examples: ban, unban,
  > delete_article, delete_comment, create_section, edit_section,
  > delete_section, approve_admin_request, reject_admin_request,
  > promote_admin, demote_admin.
- `target_entity`
  > Type of entity affected by the action. Examples: user, article, comment,
  > section, admin_request.
- `target_id`
  > ID of the affected entity. Nullable for actions that don't target a
  > specific entity.
- `details`
  > JSON string containing additional context about the action. May include
  > ban reasons, rejection reasons, or other action-specific metadata.
- `ip`
  > IP address of the administrator at the time of action for security
  > auditing.
- `user_agent`
  > Browser/client user agent string for security auditing and forensic
  > analysis.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the administrative action was performed.

### `discussion_board_sections`

Discussion board sections for topic organization with name and description.

Sections categorize articles into topic areas (e.g., Politics, Economy,
Current Affairs). Administrators create and manage sections, while all
users can browse sections and view articles within them. Each section has
a unique name and descriptive text explaining its purpose.

Sections are referenced by [discussion_board_articles](#discussion_board_articles) through the
section foreign key relationship.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `name`: Section name for topic categorization. Must be unique across all sections.
- `description`: Section description explaining the topic scope and purpose.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the section was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the section was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the section was soft deleted. Null if section is active.

### `discussion_board_section_snapshots`

Point-in-time snapshots of sections for audit trail and change tracking.
Captures the state of a section at specific moments to preserve
historical data for compliance, moderation review, and change tracking.
Each snapshot is immutable and append-only, creating a complete history
of section modifications over time.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_section_id`
  > Parent section's [discussion_board_sections.id](#discussion_board_sections). References the
  > section this snapshot belongs to.
- `name`
  > Section name at the time of snapshot. Denormalized from parent section to
  > preserve historical value.
- `description`
  > Section description at the time of snapshot. Denormalized from parent
  > section to preserve historical value.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this snapshot was created. Records the point-in-time when
  > the section state was captured.

### `discussion_board_articles`

Main article entity representing user-created content in the discussion
board. Each article belongs to exactly one section and is authored by one
member. Articles support multiple file attachments, image attachments,
and tags through separate child tables. Articles can be edited and
deleted by their authors, and administrators can delete any article for
moderation. Soft delete is supported via deleted_at timestamp for cascade
deletion tracking and audit purposes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_section_id`
  > Belonged section's [discussion_board_sections.id](#discussion_board_sections). Articles must be
  > assigned to exactly one section for topic organization.
- `discussion_board_member_id`
  > Author member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members). The registered user
  > who created and owns this article.
- `title`
  > Article title. Required field that serves as the main heading and primary
  > search target for article discovery.
- `content`
  > Article body content text. Required field containing the main discussion
  > content, supports rich text formatting.
- `created_at`
  > Article creation timestamp. Records when the article was first created,
  > used for chronological sorting and audit trail.
- `updated_at`
  > Article last update timestamp. Records when the article was last
  > modified, updated on each edit operation.
- `deleted_at`
  > Article soft deletion timestamp. Null for active articles, populated when
  > article is deleted to enable cascade deletion tracking and audit
  > compliance.

### `discussion_board_article_files`

File attachments for articles, supporting multiple files per article with
storage metadata. Each file record tracks the original filename, MIME
type, file size, and storage location. Files are managed through their
parent article and cascade delete when the article is removed. Separate
from image attachments to support different validation rules and
processing workflows.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_article_id`: Parent article's [discussion_board_articles.id](#discussion_board_articles).
- `discussion_board_member_id`: Member who uploaded the file's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members).
- `name`
  > Stored filename in the storage system, typically a UUID or hash to ensure
  > uniqueness.
- `original_name`
  > Original filename as uploaded by the user, preserved for display and
  > download purposes.
- `mime_type`
  > MIME type of the file (e.g., application/pdf, text/plain) for content
  > type validation and proper download headers.
- `size`: File size in bytes for storage quota management and upload validation.
- `path`
  > Storage path or URL where the file is located, used for file retrieval
  > and CDN access.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the file attachment was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the file attachment was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the file attachment was soft deleted, null if active.

### `discussion_board_article_images`

Image attachments for articles storing image-specific metadata including
dimensions, file size, and storage location. Each record represents one
image file attached to an article, supporting multiple images per
article. Images are managed through the parent article and cascade
deleted when the article is removed.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_article_id`: Parent article's [discussion_board_articles.id](#discussion_board_articles).
- `name`: Original filename of the uploaded image.
- `size`: File size in bytes.
- `type`: MIME type of the image file (e.g., image/jpeg, image/png).
- `url`: CDN or storage URL for accessing the image file.
- `width`: Image width in pixels.
- `height`: Image height in pixels.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the image attachment was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the image attachment was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the image attachment was soft deleted (null if active).

### `discussion_board_tags`

Reusable tag definitions for article categorization and discovery. Tags
are created on-demand when users add them to articles and can be reused
across multiple articles. Enables efficient tag-based filtering, search,
and content discovery workflows.

Tags support the article tagging system where users can attach multiple
free-text tags to their articles for better organization and
discoverability. Each unique tag name is stored once and referenced by
multiple articles through the discussion_board_article_tags junction
table.

Related entities: [discussion_board_articles](#discussion_board_articles) (tagged articles),
[discussion_board_article_tags](#discussion_board_article_tags) (many-to-many junction).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `name`
  > Tag name text for article categorization. Must be unique across all tags
  > to enable tag reuse and prevent duplication. Used for tag-based filtering
  > and search functionality.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the tag was first created. Automatically set on tag
  > creation for audit trail and chronological tracking.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the tag was last modified. Updated on each tag
  > modification to track change history.

### `discussion_board_article_tags`

Junction table establishing many-to-many relationship between articles
and tags. Enables efficient tag-based article filtering and tag reuse
across multiple articles. Each row represents a single tag assignment to
an article, with uniqueness constraint preventing duplicate tag
assignments on the same article.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_article_id`
  > Reference to the article being tagged. {@link
  > discussion_board_articles.id}.
- `discussion_board_tag_id`: Reference to the tag being applied. [discussion_board_tags.id](#discussion_board_tags).
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the tag was assigned to the article. Used for tracking tag
  > assignment order and audit purposes.

### `discussion_board_article_snapshots`

Point-in-time snapshots of article content for audit trail and change
tracking.

Captures the state of an article at specific moments, preserving title
and body content as they existed at each snapshot. Created automatically
when articles are created or modified to maintain a complete audit trail.

Used for compliance requirements, content moderation review, and tracking
content changes over time. Each snapshot is immutable once created.

Related to [discussion_board_articles](#discussion_board_articles) through a one-to-many
relationship where one article can have multiple snapshots over its
lifetime.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_article_id`
  > Parent article's [discussion_board_articles.id](#discussion_board_articles). References the
  > article this snapshot belongs to.
- `title`
  > Article title at the time of snapshot. Denormalized from the parent
  > article for historical preservation.
- `body`
  > Article content at the time of snapshot. Denormalized from the parent
  > article for historical preservation.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this snapshot was created. Represents the point-in-time
  > when the article state was captured.

### `discussion_board_comments`

Single-level comments on articles enabling discussion threads. Each
comment belongs to exactly one article and is authored by one member.
Comments are displayed in chronological order (oldest first) and support
edit/delete operations by owners and administrators. Cascade deletion
occurs when parent articles are deleted.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_article_id`
  > Parent article's [discussion_board_articles.id](#discussion_board_articles). Comments cannot
  > exist without an article.
- `discussion_board_member_id`
  > Author member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members). Only registered
  > members can post comments.
- `content`
  > Comment text content. Required field with minimum and maximum length
  > constraints per validation rules.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the comment was initially created. Used for chronological
  > sorting (oldest first).
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the comment was last modified. Updated on each edit
  > operation.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the comment was soft deleted. Null indicates active
  > comment. Set on owner deletion, admin deletion, or cascade from article
  > deletion.

### `discussion_board_comment_snapshots`

Point-in-time snapshots of comments for audit trail. Captures comment
state at each edit to preserve edit history and enable content moderation
review. Each snapshot record is immutable and append-only, creating a
complete historical record of comment modifications.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_comment_id`
  > Parent comment's [discussion_board_comments.id](#discussion_board_comments). References the
  > comment this snapshot belongs to.
- `discussion_board_member_id`
  > Author member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members) at snapshot time.
  > Denormalized for historical accuracy.
- `discussion_board_article_id`
  > Parent article's [discussion_board_articles.id](#discussion_board_articles) at snapshot time.
  > Denormalized for historical accuracy.
- `content`
  > Comment content at snapshot time. Preserves the exact text as it appeared
  > when this snapshot was created.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this snapshot was created. Records the exact moment of the
  > edit or state capture.

### `discussion_board_admin_requests`

Administrator application requests submitted by members seeking privilege
escalation. Each request includes justification reason, current status
(pending/approved/rejected), and submission timestamp. Super
administrators review and decide on requests, with decision recorded for
audit trail.

Key relationships:
- [discussion_board_members](#discussion_board_members): The member who submitted the request
- [discussion_board_admins](#discussion_board_admins): The super administrator who made the
decision (nullable until decided)
- [discussion_board_admin_request_histories](#discussion_board_admin_request_histories): Audit trail of all
status transitions

Business constraints:
- Single pending request per member (enforced by unique index on
member_id with status filter at application layer)
- Status transitions: pending → approved/rejected (immutable after decision)
- Reason text required (50-2000 characters per validation rules)

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `member_id`
  > The member who submitted the administrator application request. {@link
  > discussion_board_members.id}
- `admin_id`
  > The super administrator who reviewed and decided on this request. {@link
  > discussion_board_admins.id}
- `reason`
  > Justification text explaining why the member requests administrator
  > privileges. Required field with 50-2000 character validation.
- `status`
  > Current request status: pending (awaiting review), approved (promoted to
  > administrator), or rejected (denied). Transitions from pending to
  > approved/rejected are immutable.
- `submitted_at`
  > Timestamp when the member submitted the administrator request. Used for
  > sorting pending queue and enforcing waiting periods.
- `decided_at`
  > Timestamp when the super administrator made the decision
  > (approved/rejected). Null while status is pending.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp for audit trail.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp for change tracking.

### `discussion_board_admin_request_histories`

Audit trail recording all status transitions of administrator application
requests. Each history entry captures when a request's status changed,
which super administrator made the decision, and the reason for rejection
if applicable. This table provides complete audit compliance for
privilege escalation workflows and administrative transparency.

Related entities: [discussion_board_admin_requests](#discussion_board_admin_requests) (parent request
being audited), [discussion_board_admins](#discussion_board_admins) (super administrator who
made the decision).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_admin_request_id`
  > Parent admin request's [discussion_board_admin_requests.id](#discussion_board_admin_requests) being
  > audited.
- `deciding_admin_id`
  > Super administrator's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins) who made the
  > status decision.
- `status`
  > Request status at this transition point. Values: pending, approved,
  > rejected.
- `reason`
  > Optional reason text for rejection decisions. Null for approvals or
  > pending status.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this status transition occurred.

### `discussion_board_bans`

Active ban records that restrict user access to the platform.

Stores current bans imposed by administrators on members, including the
ban reason and timestamp. Each banned user has exactly one active ban
record at any time. When a user is unbanned, the record is soft-deleted
and an entry is added to the ban history audit trail.

Banned users cannot log in but their existing articles and comments
remain visible per content preservation policy. Administrators can view
the banned users list with ban reasons for transparency.

Related entities: [discussion_board_members](#discussion_board_members) (banned user), {@link
discussion_board_admins} (enforcing administrator), {@link
discussion_board_ban_histories} (audit trail).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `member_id`
  > Banned member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members). The user whose
  > access is restricted by this ban.
- `admin_id`
  > Enforcing administrator's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins). The
  > administrator who imposed this ban.
- `reason`
  > Ban reason explaining why the user was banned. Required for
  > administrative transparency and must meet minimum/maximum length
  > validation requirements.
- `banned_at`
  > Timestamp when the ban was imposed. Automatically recorded at ban
  > creation and immutable thereafter for audit integrity.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp. Set when user is unbanned to preserve audit
  > history while marking ban as inactive.

### `discussion_board_ban_histories`

Audit trail of all ban and unban events with timestamps and
action-specific reasons.

This table maintains a complete history of all ban-related actions for
compliance and transparency. Each record captures either a ban or unban
event, including the action type and reason provided by the administrator
at the time of the action.

Related to [discussion_board_bans](#discussion_board_bans) for the parent ban record (which
contains member and administrator references), {@link
discussion_board_members} for the affected user account (via ban
relationship), and [discussion_board_admins](#discussion_board_admins) for the administrator
who performed the action (via ban relationship).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_ban_id`
  > Reference to the parent ban record. [discussion_board_bans.id](#discussion_board_bans).
  > Member and administrator references are accessible through this
  > relationship.
- `action`
  > Type of action performed: 'banned' or 'unbanned'. Distinguishes between
  > ban imposition and ban removal events.
- `reason`
  > Action-specific reason provided by the administrator. Required for ban
  > events, optional for unban events. Captures the context for this specific
  > history entry.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the ban or unban action was recorded. Immutable after
  > creation for audit integrity.

instruction:
User Account
- Users sign up with email and password
- Users log in with email and password
- Users can change their password
- Users can delete their account (all their articles and comments are also deleted)

User Profile
- Each user has a profile with: display name and bio text
- Users can edit their display name and bio
- Users can view other users' profiles
- A user's profile shows:
  - Their display name and bio
  - A list of all articles they have written
  - A list of all comments they have written

Sections
- The board is divided into sections (e.g., Politics, Economy, Current Affairs)
- Sections are created and managed by administrators only
- Each section has: name and description
- Users can view the list of all sections
- Users can browse articles within a specific section

Articles
- Users can create articles in any section
- Every article has:
  - Title (required)
  - Content (required, text)
  - Section (required, must choose one section)
- Users can attach files to their articles
- Users can attach images to their articles
- Multiple files and images can be attached to a single article
- Users can add tags to their articles (free text, multiple tags allowed)
- Users can edit their own articles (title, content, attachments, tags)
- Users can delete their own articles

Article List
- Users can view the list of articles in a section
- The list is paginated
- Each article in the list shows: title, author, tags, comment count, and time posted
- The list does not show the full content (only title)
- Users can sort articles by:
  - Newest first
  - Oldest first

Viewing an Article
- Users can view a single article with its full content
- The article page shows: title, author, content, attachments, tags, and time posted
- Users can download attached files and images

Searching Articles
- Users can search articles by title or content
- Search results are paginated
- Users can filter articles by tags

Comments
- Users can write comments on articles
- Comments are single-level only (no nested replies)
- Users can view all comments on an article
- Comments are sorted by oldest first
- Each comment shows: author, content, and time posted
- Users can edit their own comments
- Users can delete their own comments

Administrator System
- Any user can submit a request to become an administrator
- The request includes a reason (text)
- Super administrators can view the list of pending requests
- Super administrators can approve or reject requests
- When approved, the user becomes a regular administrator

Administrator Grades
- There are two grades: regular administrator and super administrator
- Super administrators can promote regular administrators to super administrator
- Super administrators can demote other super administrators to regular administrator
- Super administrators cannot demote themselves

Administrator Capabilities
- Administrators can do everything regular users can do (write articles, comments, etc.)
- Administrators can create, edit, and delete sections
- Administrators can delete any article
- Administrators can delete any comment
- Administrators can ban users
- Administrators can unban users
- Administrators can view the list of banned users

Banning
- Banned users cannot log in to the platform
- Banned users' existing articles and comments remain visible
- When a user is banned, a reason is recorded
- Administrators can view the ban reason for each banned user

operations.specification: Create a new guest account using device fingerprint for anonymous browsing access. Generate a unique device fingerprint if not provided, or use the supplied fingerprint to identify returning guests. Create a new guest session with connection metadata (IP address, page URL, referrer) and set expiration timestamp based on session duration policy. operations.description:
Register a new guest user for anonymous browsing access to the discussion board platform.

This endpoint creates a guest account identified by a unique device fingerprint, enabling temporary session management without requiring traditional email/password authentication. The device fingerprint is generated from browser/device characteristics to distinguish anonymous visitors. If no fingerprint is provided, the system generates one automatically.

The operation creates a new record in the discussion_board_guests table with the device_fingerprint field set to the provided or generated value. It also creates an initial session record in discussion_board_guest_sessions with connection metadata including the client IP address, initial page URL (href), and HTTP referrer header for traffic source tracking.

Upon successful registration, the endpoint returns JWT access and refresh tokens in the IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized response structure. The access token grants temporary browsing permissions, while the refresh token enables session renewal before expiration. Session expiration is configured according to platform policy and stored in the expired_at column of the guest session record.

Guests have read-only access to sections, articles, and comments but cannot create content, manage profiles, or access member-only features. This operation is the entry point for anonymous users to access the discussion board platform.

responseBody.description: JWT tokens and guest information for authenticated browsing

operations.description:
Refresh an existing guest session to obtain new JWT access and refresh tokens.

This endpoint enables guests to renew their authentication tokens before the current session expires, maintaining continuous anonymous browsing access without requiring re-registration. The operation validates the provided refresh token against existing guest sessions in the discussion_board_guest_sessions table.

The refresh token is checked against the session records to find a matching valid session. The system verifies that the session's expired_at timestamp has not passed, ensuring the session is still active. If the session is found and valid, new JWT access and refresh tokens are generated with fresh expiration times according to the platform's session duration policy.

The session record in discussion_board_guest_sessions is updated with the new expired_at timestamp to extend the session lifetime. This enables guests to maintain their browsing session across extended periods of activity without losing their anonymous identity.

If the refresh token is invalid, expired, or not found, the operation returns an authentication error indicating the guest must re-join to obtain new credentials. This ensures expired sessions are properly terminated and prevents unauthorized access using stale tokens.

responseBody.description: New JWT tokens for continued authenticated browsing

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of member accounts from the discussion board platform.

This operation provides comprehensive search capabilities for discovering user profiles across the platform. Users can search by display name using partial matching, filter by account status (active, suspended, deleted), and navigate through results using cursor-based pagination. The endpoint supports sorting by registration date (newest or oldest first) to help users find recently joined members or browse the community chronologically.

For guests and regular members, this endpoint enables profile discovery and community exploration. Each result includes essential profile information: display name, bio preview, account status, and registration timestamp. The summary format optimizes list display performance while providing sufficient context for users to identify profiles of interest.

Administrators have enhanced capabilities through this endpoint, including the ability to filter by all account statuses for user management purposes. This supports administrative workflows such as reviewing suspended accounts, monitoring community growth, and identifying users for potential administrative actions.

The operation integrates with the profile viewing system - users can retrieve detailed profile information including article and comment history by using the member ID obtained from this list in the GET /members/{memberId} endpoint. Search results respect privacy and access control policies, ensuring appropriate visibility based on the requesting user's authorization level.

Validation ensures search queries meet length requirements and pagination parameters stay within configured limits. The endpoint handles edge cases including empty result sets, invalid status filters, and concurrent account state changes gracefully.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query discussion_board_members table with pagination and filtering support.

Apply search filters on display_name using trigram similarity for partial matching (GIN index on display_name). Filter by status field (active, suspended, deleted) - guests and members can only see active accounts, administrators can see all statuses.

Support cursor-based pagination using created_at timestamp for efficient large dataset navigation. Default page size 20, maximum 100 items per page.

Sort by created_at ascending (oldest first) or descending (newest first). Default sort is descending.

Join with discussion_board_admins to enrich results with administrator grade information for admin users viewing the list.

Exclude soft-deleted accounts (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) from results for non-administrator users. Administrators can optionally include deleted accounts for audit purposes.

Handle concurrent account status changes by reading consistent snapshots. Apply row-level security based on requesting user's role.

Return IDiscussionBoardMember.ISummary for each member containing: id, display_name, bio (truncated), status, created_at, and isAdmin flag.

Error handling: Return 400 for invalid status values, invalid pagination parameters, or search query exceeding maximum length. Return 401 for unauthenticated requests attempting to access non-public member information.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of member profile summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for member list query

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific member's public profile information by their unique identifier.

This operation returns comprehensive profile data including the member's display name shown publicly on articles and comments, biography text for personal description, and account status indicating active, suspended, or deleted state. The profile also includes temporal metadata such as account creation timestamp and last update timestamp.

The endpoint supports public profile viewing accessible to all actors including guests, members, and administrators. Guests can browse profiles without authentication as part of public content discovery. Members can view other members' profiles to see their discussion contributions. Administrators can view profiles for moderation and user management purposes.

Sensitive authentication fields such as email address and password hash are intentionally excluded from the response to protect user privacy and security. The profile response focuses on publicly shareable information that facilitates community interaction and user discovery within the discussion board platform.

Related operations include PATCH /members for retrieving the authenticated user's own profile with additional details, PATCH /members/{memberId}/articles for listing articles written by the member, and PATCH /members/{memberId}/comments for listing comments posted by the member.

Query discussion_board_members table by primary key UUID.

Validate memberId is valid UUID format. Return 404 if member not found or if deleted_at is not null (soft deleted account).

Select fields: id, display_name, bio, status, created_at, updated_at. Exclude sensitive fields: email, password_hash.

Join with discussion_board_articles to count total articles authored. Join with discussion_board_comments to count total comments posted. Include these counts in response for profile summary.

Check member status: if status is 'suspended' or 'deleted', still return profile but may include status indicator for API consumers.

Apply data isolation rules: profile data is public, no ownership check required for viewing.

Cache profile data with appropriate TTL to reduce database load for frequently viewed profiles.

responseBody.description: Member profile information with public details

operations.description:
Update the authenticated member's profile information including display name and biography text.

This operation allows authenticated members to modify their profile by updating their display name and bio text stored in the discussion_board_members table. The display name is a required field shown publicly on articles, comments, and profile pages - visible to all users including guests. The bio text is an optional personal description visible on the member's profile page.

The operation requires authentication with a valid member session token and only allows members to update their own profile. Attempting to update another user's profile will be rejected with an authorization error. The display name field must be provided in every update request and is validated against character limits and content restrictions. The bio field is optional and can be omitted, set to null, or updated with new text content.

Profile changes are reflected immediately across all content authored by the member, including articles and comments where the display name appears. The updated_at timestamp in the discussion_board_members table is automatically updated to the current timestamp when the profile is modified.

Validation rules applied:
- Display name: Must meet character limits and content restrictions defined in User Validation Rules
- Bio text: Must not exceed maximum length defined in User Validation Rules

Related operations include GET /discussionBoard/member/profile for viewing the current user's profile and PATCH /discussionBoard/members for searching and viewing other users' profiles.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update the authenticated member's profile in the discussion_board_members table.

1. Extract member ID from authenticated session token
2. Validate request body:
   - display_name: required, must be non-empty string
   - bio: optional, can be null or string
3. Validate display_name meets content policies (no prohibited content)
4. Update discussion_board_members record:
   - SET display_name = request.display_name
   - SET bio = request.bio (or keep existing if not provided)
   - SET updated_at = current timestamp
5. Return updated member record with new profile data
6. Handle concurrent update conflicts with optimistic locking

Authentication: Requires valid member session token. Guest users and administrators must authenticate as members to update their profile.

responseBody.description: Updated member profile information with new display name and bio

requestBody.description: Profile update data containing display name and optional biography text

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of active administrator accounts in the discussion board platform.

This operation provides administrators with the ability to view all active administrator accounts on the platform, including both regular administrators and super administrators. The endpoint supports filtering by administrator grade level, allowing users to search for specific grade types or view all administrators regardless of grade.

The response includes administrator summary information optimized for list displays, showing the administrator's grade level, promotion date (created_at), and associated member display name. This enables administrators to understand the current administrator hierarchy and identify peers for collaboration on platform governance tasks.

Only active administrators are included in the results - records with deleted_at set (soft-deleted administrators whose privileges were revoked) are excluded. The deleted_at field being null indicates an active administrator, while a non-null deleted_at timestamp indicates the administrator privileges have been revoked.

This operation requires administrator authentication as per the admin actor definition with platform governance capabilities. Regular members and guests cannot access the administrator list. The endpoint supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options by grade level, promotion date, or member display name.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query discussion_board_admins table with pagination and filtering. Apply grade filter if provided (regular or super). Exclude soft-deleted records where deleted_at is not null. Join with discussion_board_members to include member display name and email in summary. Support sorting by grade, created_at (promotion date), or member display name. Return cursor-based or offset pagination with total count. Filter out administrators with deleted_at set. Validate administrator authentication before query execution.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of active administrator summaries with grade and member information

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for administrator list query

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific administrator account.

This operation returns comprehensive administrator profile data including the administrator's grade level (regular or super), associated member account information, and account lifecycle timestamps. The administrator grade determines privilege scope: regular administrators can manage sections, delete content, and ban users; super administrators have elevated powers including approving admin requests and managing other administrators' grades.

The response includes the administrator's ID, grade level, creation timestamp, last update timestamp, and the associated member's profile information (email, display name, bio, account status). This endpoint is useful for viewing administrator details, verifying administrator status, and displaying administrator profiles to authorized users.

Administrators are promoted from existing members through an approval process, maintaining a 1:1 relationship with the original member account. The administrator record preserves the member's identity while granting elevated permissions. If the administrator has been soft deleted (deleted_at is not null), the operation will return a 404 error indicating the administrator is no longer active.

This operation requires administrator authentication. Only users with administrator role can access this endpoint to view administrator account details. This restriction ensures that sensitive administrator information including grade levels and account lifecycle data is only visible to authorized personnel with platform governance responsibilities.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the discussion_board_admins table by the adminId path parameter.

1. Validate adminId is a valid UUID format
2. Query discussion_board_admins WHERE id = adminId AND deleted_at IS NULL
3. Join with discussion_board_members on member_id to include member profile information
4. Return the administrator record with embedded member data (display_name, bio, email, status)
5. Handle not found: if no administrator exists with the given ID, return 404
6. Handle soft deleted: if deleted_at is not null, return 404 or indicate inactive status
7. Include grade information to indicate privilege level (regular or super)
8. Include timestamps: created_at (when admin request was approved), updated_at (last grade change or update)

Authorization: Require authenticated user (member or admin). Guests may have read-only access to basic administrator profile information.

responseBody.description: Administrator profile with member information

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of user sessions across the discussion board platform.

This administrative operation provides comprehensive session monitoring capabilities for security audit and compliance purposes. Administrators can search sessions by user identifier, IP address, session status (active/expired), and creation time ranges. The endpoint aggregates sessions from member, administrator, and guest session tables.

Each session record includes connection metadata (IP address, referrer, href) and temporal fields (created_at, expired_at) for audit trail analysis. This supports security monitoring, suspicious activity detection, and compliance with authentication logging requirements.

Access is restricted to administrators only. Regular members and guests cannot view session information. The operation supports pagination for large result sets and sorting by session creation time or expiration time.

Related operations: GET /sessions/{sessionId} retrieves detailed session information. Session invalidation is handled through authentication logout flows, not this endpoint.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query session tables (discussion_board_member_sessions, discussion_board_admin_sessions, discussion_board_guest_sessions) with pagination and filtering.

Apply search filters on: user ID (member_id, admin_id, or guest_id), IP address partial match, session status (active if expired_at > now, expired otherwise), creation date range, expiration date range.

Join with discussion_board_members and discussion_board_admins to retrieve user display names and account status.

Filter out soft-deleted administrator records (deleted_at IS NULL for active admins).

Return cursor-based pagination with session summary including: session ID, user type (member/admin/guest), user display name, IP address, creation time, expiration time, status (active/expired).

Sort by created_at DESC by default (newest sessions first). Support sorting by expired_at ASC (sessions expiring soonest).

Enforce administrator-only access control. Reject requests from non-administrator actors.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of session summaries with metadata

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for session filtering

operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query discussion_board_member_sessions table by session ID. Validate the requesting user has permission to view this session (either owns the session or has administrator privileges). Join with discussion_board_members to verify ownership if needed. Return session details including connection metadata (IP, href, referrer) and temporal fields (created_at, expired_at). Handle case where session doesn't exist by returning 404. Ensure banned users cannot access session information even with valid session ID.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific member session owned by the authenticated member.

This operation provides members access to their own session metadata including connection details and temporal information. Sessions are automatically created during the authentication flow when members log in to the discussion board platform. Each session record contains connection metadata such as IP address, initial page URL (href), and HTTP referrer for security audit purposes.

The session details include creation timestamp marking when the authentication occurred and expiration timestamp indicating when the session becomes invalid. This information enables members to monitor their account activity and verify their login history.

Access is restricted to the session owner - members can only retrieve sessions associated with their own account. The system validates ownership by matching the session's discussion_board_member_id with the authenticated member's ID. Attempting to access another member's session will result in authorization failure.

This operation complements the authentication flow by providing transparency into active and historical sessions. Members can detect unauthorized access by reviewing session details and identifying unfamiliar connection metadata.

responseBody.description: Detailed session information including connection metadata and temporal fields

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of discussion board articles from the discussion_board_articles table with comprehensive search and sorting capabilities.

This operation provides article discovery functionality including text search across title and content fields, filtering by section (discussion_board_section_id), tags (via discussion_board_article_tags junction table), and author (discussion_board_member_id). The endpoint supports offset-based pagination for efficient navigation through result sets.

Search functionality utilizes PostgreSQL gin_trgm_ops trigram indexes on title and content columns for efficient text matching. Tag filtering matches articles that have any of the specified tags through the discussion_board_article_tags junction table. Section filtering restricts results to articles within a specific discussion_board_sections record.

Each article in the response includes essential summary information: title, author details (joined from discussion_board_members), associated tags, comment count (aggregated from discussion_board_comments), and created_at timestamp. The full content field is not included in list results to optimize performance and reduce payload size.

Authorization: Available to all actors (guest, member, admin). Banned users cannot access this endpoint. Articles with deleted_at timestamp populated are automatically excluded from results (soft delete filtering).

Related operations: GET /articles/{articleId} retrieves full article details including content and attachments. PATCH /sections/{sectionId}/articles filters articles by a specific section.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query discussion_board_articles table with pagination, search filters, and sorting.

Search Implementation:
- Use PostgreSQL gin_trgm_ops trigram indexes on title and content for efficient text search
- Apply ILIKE pattern matching for search queries
- Support combined title/content search when both provided

Filtering Logic:
- Section filter: WHERE discussion_board_section_id = {sectionId}
- Tag filter: JOIN discussion_board_article_tags and discussion_board_tags, filter by tag names
- Author filter: WHERE discussion_board_member_id = {authorId}
- Exclude soft-deleted: WHERE deleted_at IS NULL

Sorting Options:
- 'newest': ORDER BY created_at DESC (default)
- 'oldest': ORDER BY created_at ASC

Pagination:
- Implement cursor-based pagination using created_at and id for stable ordering
- Support configurable page size with reasonable limits (e.g., 10-100 items per page)
- Return pagination metadata: total count, current page, has_next, has_previous

Response Assembly:
- Join with discussion_board_members for author display name
- Aggregate tags via discussion_board_article_tags junction
- Count comments via discussion_board_comments with GROUP BY
- Map to IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary DTO

Edge Cases:
- Empty search query returns all articles (no filtering)
- Non-existent section/tag/author returns empty result set
- Handle concurrent article deletion during query gracefully

responseBody.description: Paginated list of article summaries with search metadata and pagination information

requestBody.description: Search criteria, filters, and pagination parameters for article list query including text search, section/tag/author filters, sort order, and pagination controls

operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the discussion_board_articles table by the article's UUID primary key. Join with discussion_board_members to retrieve author information including display name. Include related file attachments from discussion_board_article_files, image attachments from discussion_board_article_images, and tags through discussion_board_article_tags junction table joined with discussion_board_tags. Apply soft delete filtering to exclude articles where deleted_at is not null unless the requester is an administrator. Return the complete article object with all nested relationships. Handle 404 error when article ID does not exist or article is soft deleted.
operations.description:
Retrieve a single article by its unique identifier with complete details including title, content, author information, attachments, and tags.

This endpoint provides full article information for display on the article detail page. The response includes the article's title, content text, creation timestamp, and all associated metadata. Author information is included with the member's display name for proper attribution. File attachments and image attachments are returned with their storage URLs for download access. Tags assigned to the article are included for categorization and discovery purposes.

All users including guests can access this endpoint to view articles. Soft-deleted articles are not accessible through this endpoint and will return a 404 Not Found response. The article must exist in the database and not have been deleted by the author or an administrator.

Related operations include PATCH /articles for searching and listing articles with filters, and the section browsing endpoints for discovering articles within specific topic categories.

responseBody.description: Complete article information with author, attachments, and tags

operations.description:
Create a new discussion board article with title, content, section assignment, and optional attachments.

This operation enables authenticated members to create articles within the discussion board system. Each article must be assigned to exactly one section for topic organization and categorization. The article serves as the foundation for community discussion and debate on various topics.

The creation process supports multiple file attachments and image attachments through URI references. File attachments store metadata including original filename, MIME type, and file size for proper download handling. Image attachments include dimension information (width and height) for optimal display rendering.

Tags can be assigned to articles for improved discoverability and content organization. The system automatically creates new tags if they don't exist, or reuses existing tags with matching names. This enables efficient tag-based filtering and search functionality across the platform.

Only authenticated members can create articles. Guest users must register and log in before accessing this endpoint. The article author is automatically set to the authenticated member's ID from the session context.

Upon successful creation, the article is immediately visible in the section's article list. The operation returns the complete article entity including all metadata, attachment information, and tag assignments.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new article record in discussion_board_articles table with the following steps:

1. Validate authentication: Ensure request is from authenticated member (discussion_board_members). Reject guest users with 401 Unauthorized.

2. Validate section existence: Query discussion_board_sections by provided sectionId. Return 404 Not Found if section doesn't exist or is soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null).

3. Validate required fields:
   - title: non-empty string, minimum 1 character, maximum 200 characters
   - content: non-empty string, minimum 1 character, maximum 100000 characters
   - sectionId: valid UUID format

4. Validate optional attachments:
   - fileUrls: array of valid URI strings (string & tags.Format<"uri">)
   - imageUrls: array of valid URI strings (string & tags.Format<"uri">)
   - tags: array of non-empty strings, deduplicate before processing

5. Create article record:
   - Generate new UUID for article id
   - Set discussion_board_section_id from request
   - Set discussion_board_member_id from authenticated session
   - Set title and content from request
   - Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp
   - Set deleted_at to null

6. Process file attachments (if fileUrls provided):
   - For each file URL, create discussion_board_article_files record
   - Extract filename from URL or use provided metadata
   - Set discussion_board_article_id to new article's id
   - Set discussion_board_member_id from session
   - Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp

7. Process image attachments (if imageUrls provided):
   - For each image URL, create discussion_board_article_images record
   - Extract or compute image dimensions (width, height)
   - Set discussion_board_article_id to new article's id
   - Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp

8. Process tags:
   - For each unique tag name:
     a. Query discussion_board_tags by name (case-insensitive)
     b. If exists, use existing tag id
     c. If not exists, create new tag with generated UUID and current timestamp
     d. Create discussion_board_article_tags record linking article and tag

9. Return complete article entity with all relationships loaded:
   - Article base fields (id, title, content, timestamps)
   - Section information (joined from discussion_board_sections)
   - Author information (joined from discussion_board_members)
   - File attachments array (from discussion_board_article_files)
   - Image attachments array (from discussion_board_article_images)
   - Tags array (joined through discussion_board_article_tags to discussion_board_tags)

Transaction boundary: Steps 5-8 must execute within a single database transaction. If any step fails, rollback all changes to maintain data consistency.

Error handling:
- 401 Unauthorized: User not authenticated as member
- 404 Not Found: Section not found or deleted
- 400 Bad Request: Validation errors (missing required fields, invalid formats)
- 500 Internal Server Error: Database transaction failure

responseBody.description: Complete article entity with all metadata, attachments, and tag assignments

requestBody.description: Article creation data including required title, content, section assignment, and optional file attachments, image attachments, and tags

prerequisites.description: Section must exist before an article can be assigned to it. The sectionId in article creation references discussion_board_sections table via foreign key constraint.

operations.description:
Update an existing article's content, title, section assignment, and metadata.

This operation allows the article's author to modify their article's title, content text, and section assignment. The article must exist and be owned by the requesting user. Administrators can also update any article for moderation purposes.

The update operation replaces the article's title, content, and section fields with the provided values. Attachments (files and images) and tags are managed through separate child endpoints - this operation focuses on the core article properties. The updated_at timestamp is automatically updated to reflect the modification time.

Authorization requires the user to be either the article's author (discussion_board_member_id matches authenticated user) or an administrator with elevated permissions. Banned users cannot update articles. If the article has been soft deleted (deleted_at is set), the update will be rejected.

Related operations: GET /articles/{articleId} retrieves the article before editing. PATCH /articles supports search and filtering. POST /articles creates new articles. DELETE /articles/{articleId} removes an article.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Query discussion_board_articles table by articleId UUID. Verify the article exists and is not soft deleted (deleted_at is null). Check authorization: authenticated user must match discussion_board_member_id OR have administrator role. Validate title is non-empty and within length constraints. Validate content is non-empty and within length constraints. Validate discussion_board_section_id references an existing, non-deleted section. Update title, content, discussion_board_section_id, and updated_at timestamp in a single transaction. Return the updated article entity with all fields. Handle concurrent update conflicts using optimistic locking on updated_at. Reject if article is soft deleted or user lacks permission.

responseBody.description: Updated article entity with all fields

prerequisites.description: Section must exist before being referenced by an article's section assignment
Article must be created before it can be updated

operations.description:
Soft delete an article by marking it as deleted in the discussion board.

This operation sets the deleted_at timestamp on the article record, marking it as deleted while maintaining the data for audit trail compliance. The soft delete triggers cascade deletion of all associated child entities including file attachments, image attachments, tag assignments, and comments.

Only the article's author (owner) or administrators can delete an article. Regular users attempting to delete articles they don't own will receive an authorization error. Administrators can delete any article for moderation purposes regardless of ownership.

When an article is soft deleted, the deleted_at timestamp is populated and all related discussion_board_article_files, discussion_board_article_images, discussion_board_article_tags, and discussion_board_comments records are cascade deleted through database foreign key constraints. The article record remains in the database with the deleted_at timestamp set, enabling audit tracking and compliance with data retention requirements.

This operation is irreversible through the API. Once the deleted_at timestamp is set, the article and all its associated content cannot be recovered.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete article by setting deleted_at timestamp (soft delete).

1. Verify article exists and is not already deleted
2. Check authorization: allow if current user is article owner (discussion_board_member_id matches) OR has administrator role
3. Begin database transaction
4. Set deleted_at = current timestamp on discussion_board_articles record
5. Cascade delete triggers automatically remove:
   - discussion_board_article_files (onDelete: Cascade)
   - discussion_board_article_images (onDelete: Cascade)
   - discussion_board_article_tags (onDelete: Cascade)
   - discussion_board_comments (onDelete: Cascade)
6. Commit transaction
7. Return 204 No Content on success

Error handling:
- 404 if article not found or already deleted
- 403 if user is not owner and not administrator
- 409 if concurrent modification detected

prerequisites.description: Section must be created before articles can be assigned to it
Article must exist before it can be deleted

operations.description:
Permanently remove an article from the discussion board.

This operation deletes an article and triggers cascade deletion of all associated child entities including file attachments, image attachments, tag assignments, and comments. The article soft delete timestamp (deleted_at) is set to mark the record as deleted while maintaining audit trail compliance.

Only the article's author (owner) or administrators can delete an article. Regular users attempting to delete articles they don't own will receive an authorization error. Administrators can delete any article for moderation purposes regardless of ownership.

When an article is deleted, all related discussion_board_article_files, discussion_board_article_images, discussion_board_article_tags, and discussion_board_comments records are cascade deleted. The article's deleted_at timestamp is populated to enable audit tracking and cascade deletion compliance.

This operation is irreversible. Once deleted, the article and all its associated content cannot be recovered through the API.
operations.name: erase

2. Check authorization: allow if current user is article owner (discussion_board_member_id matches) OR has administrator role

4. Set deleted_at = current timestamp on discussion_board_articles record
5. Cascade delete triggers automatically remove:
   - discussion_board_article_files (onDelete: Cascade)
   - discussion_board_article_images (onDelete: Cascade)
   - discussion_board_article_tags (onDelete: Cascade)
   - discussion_board_comments (onDelete: Cascade)
6. Commit transaction
7. Return 204 No Content on success

Error handling:
- 404 if article not found or already deleted
- 403 if user is not owner and not administrator
- 409 if concurrent modification detected

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of comments for a specific article in chronological order.

This operation returns all active comments associated with the specified article, sorted by creation timestamp in oldest-first order to maintain discussion thread continuity. Each comment includes the author's display name, comment content, and creation timestamp for display in the article's discussion section.

Comments are single-level only with no nested replies supported. The response is paginated to handle articles with large numbers of comments efficiently. Only comments from non-deleted articles are accessible, and soft-deleted comments are automatically filtered from results.

Guest users can view all comments on accessible articles. Member users can additionally create, edit, and delete their own comments through separate endpoints. Administrators have full moderation capabilities including deletion of any comment.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query discussion_board_comments table filtered by discussion_board_article_id matching the path parameter. Join with discussion_board_members to retrieve author display_name for each comment. Filter out soft-deleted comments (deleted_at IS NOT NULL). Order by created_at ASC for oldest-first chronological display. Apply pagination with cursor or offset-based strategy. Return summary DTO with essential comment fields optimized for list display. Ensure article exists and is not soft-deleted before returning comments.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of comment summaries for the article
