operations.description:
Retrieve a specific comment on an article by its unique identifier.

This operation returns detailed information about a single comment including the comment content, author information (display name), creation timestamp, and last update timestamp. The comment must belong to the specified article, ensuring proper contextual access.

Comments are single-level discussion entries that allow users to provide feedback on articles. Each comment is authored by a registered member and displays the author's public display name. The comment content is required and subject to minimum and maximum length validation rules.

This endpoint supports viewing individual comments in detail, which is useful when navigating directly to a specific comment or when comment-specific actions are needed. The response includes the complete comment record with all metadata from the discussion_board_comments table including the deleted_at timestamp for soft delete tracking.

Authorization: Guests can view comments on accessible articles. Members can view all comments. Banned users' comments remain visible per platform policy. If the comment or article has been soft deleted (deleted_at timestamp is set), access is restricted to administrators only.

Related operations: PATCH /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}/comments retrieves the list of all comments on an article sorted oldest first. PUT /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId} updates an existing comment. DELETE /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId} removes a comment.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the discussion_board_comments table by comment ID with article context validation.

1. Validate that the articleId exists in discussion_board_articles table and is not soft deleted (deleted_at is null)
2. Query discussion_board_comments where id equals commentId AND discussion_board_article_id equals articleId
3. Join with discussion_board_members to retrieve author display_name
4. Verify the comment is not soft deleted (deleted_at is null) unless requester is administrator
5. Return the comment record with author information

Handle edge cases:
- Article not found: return 404
- Comment not found: return 404
- Comment belongs to different article: return 404
- Article or comment soft deleted: return 404 for non-admin users
- Banned user accessing: allow read access to comments

Use UUID format validation for both path parameters. Ensure the join with members table handles deleted author accounts gracefully (show anonymous indicator if member is deleted).

responseBody.description: Detailed comment information including author details and timestamps

operations.description:
Create a new comment on an article in the discussion board.

This operation allows authenticated members to post single-level comments on articles. The comment is associated with the specified article and the authenticated member who creates it. Comments are displayed in chronological order (oldest first) on the article page.

Only registered members can create comments. Guest users and banned users are not permitted to post comments. The article must exist and not be deleted for the comment to be created successfully.

The comment content is required and must meet minimum and maximum length validation rules. Upon successful creation, the system records the creation timestamp and returns the complete comment object including author information.

Comments support edit and delete operations by their authors. Administrators can also delete any comment for moderation purposes. When an article is deleted, all associated comments are cascade deleted.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Validate the articleId exists in discussion_board_articles table and deleted_at is null. Verify the authenticated user is a member (not guest) and not banned. Validate comment content meets minimum and maximum length requirements. Insert new record into discussion_board_comments table with: discussion_board_article_id from path parameter, discussion_board_member_id from authenticated session, content from request body, created_at and updated_at set to current timestamp, deleted_at as null. Return the created comment with author information joined from discussion_board_members table.

operations.name: update

Validate user is either the comment owner (discussion_board_member_id matches authenticated user) or an administrator. Update content field and set updated_at to current timestamp. Preserve created_at and deleted_at fields. Return updated comment with member and article relationships. Handle concurrent edit conflicts with optimistic locking on updated_at timestamp.
operations.description:
Update an existing comment on an article. This operation allows comment owners or administrators to modify the comment content while preserving the original creation timestamp.

The comment must belong to the specified article, and the requesting user must be either the comment author or an administrator. Only the content field can be modified; the system automatically updates the updated_at timestamp to track modification time.

Comments support soft deletion through the deleted_at field. This update operation cannot restore deleted comments. If the comment has been deleted, the operation will fail. The article association and author cannot be changed through this endpoint.

Administrators can update any comment regardless of ownership for moderation purposes. Regular members can only update their own comments. The updated comment is returned with full details including author information and timestamps.

Comment must be created before it can be updated. This prerequisite creates the specific comment entity that will be modified by the update operation, establishing the article-comment relationship.

operations.description:
Delete a specific comment from a discussion board article.

This operation removes a comment from the article's comment list, making it no longer visible to any user. The comment is soft-deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp in the database, which preserves the record for audit trail and cascade deletion tracking purposes. However, the API does not provide any mechanism to recover or restore deleted comments - once deleted, the comment is permanently inaccessible through the application.

Only the comment's author (the member who created it) or an administrator can delete a comment. Regular members can only delete their own comments, while administrators have moderation authority to delete any comment regardless of ownership. The articleId path parameter ensures the comment belongs to the specified article before deletion is processed.

When a comment is deleted, the parent article remains intact and all other comments on the article are preserved. The comment is removed from chronological display (oldest-first ordering) and no longer contributes to the article's comment count. This operation implements the business rule that comment deletion is permanent from the user's perspective, even though the database retains the record with a deleted_at timestamp for audit compliance.

If the comment does not exist, has already been deleted, the user is not the comment author (and not an administrator), or the comment does not belong to the specified article, the request is rejected with an appropriate error response.

3. Check authorization: current user must be either the comment author (discussion_board_member_id matches authenticated user) or an administrator
4. Verify the comment is not already deleted (deleted_at is null)
5. Set deleted_at to current timestamp in a database transaction
6. Update the parent article's comment count if cached
7. Return success response

Edge cases:
- Comment not found: return 404
- Comment already deleted: return 404 or 410
- Unauthorized (not author, not admin): return 403
- Article not found: return 404
- Concurrent deletion: use optimistic locking with updated_at timestamp

The endpoint respects the member's account status - comments from suspended or deleted members may have restricted visibility based on viewer permissions.

Guest users can access this endpoint to view public comment histories. Member users can view any other member's comment list. The requesting member can also view their own comment history through this endpoint.

Each section in the response includes essential information such as the section name, description, creation timestamp, and optionally the count of articles within that section.

This operation is commonly used as a prerequisite for browsing articles by section. Users typically retrieve the sections list first, then navigate to a specific section to view its articles. This operation enables administrators to create new sections that organize articles into distinct topic areas such as Politics, Economy, or Current Affairs. Each section serves as a container for related articles, providing community structure and content discovery capabilities.

The section creation requires both a name and description. The name must be unique across all sections and identifies the section's focus area. The description explains the section's purpose and scope to help users understand what type of content belongs in the section.

Only administrators can create sections. Regular users and guests do not have permission to create sections. When a section is created, it becomes immediately available for article categorization and appears in the sections list.

The system automatically generates a UUID for the section id and records the created_at and updated_at timestamps. The section is created in an active state with deleted_at set to null.

Only administrators have permission to update sections. Regular members and guests cannot modify section properties. The section name must remain unique across all sections - attempting to use a name that already exists will result in a conflict error.

The updated section is returned in the response with all current properties including the updated timestamp. This operation does not affect articles already assigned to the section - they remain associated with the section after the update.

This operation provides access to the audit trail of section modifications, allowing administrators to track how a section's name and description have changed over time. Each snapshot represents an immutable, point-in-time capture of the section's state, created automatically when section modifications occur.

The snapshots are stored in the discussion_board_section_snapshots table, which maintains an append-only history linked to the parent section through the discussion_board_section_id foreign key. Each snapshot preserves the name and description values as they existed at the time of capture, along with the created_at timestamp indicating when the snapshot was recorded.

This endpoint supports filtering by date range to help administrators review changes within specific time periods. Results are paginated to handle potentially large historical records efficiently. The snapshots are indexed by discussion_board_section_id and created_at for optimal query performance.

Access to section snapshots is restricted to administrators only, as this audit trail data is used for compliance, moderation review, and change tracking purposes. Regular members and guests cannot access historical section data.

The sectionId path parameter must correspond to an existing section in the discussion_board_sections table. If the section has been soft deleted (deleted_at is not null), snapshots may still be accessible for audit purposes depending on business rules.

Snapshots are automatically generated when sections are modified, creating an append-only history of all changes. This endpoint allows administrators to review past section configurations, verify when changes occurred, and maintain transparency in platform governance. The snapshot record includes the `id` (unique identifier), `discussion_board_section_id` (reference to the parent section), `name` (section name at snapshot time), `description` (section description at snapshot time), and `created_at` (timestamp when the snapshot was captured).

This operation is restricted to administrators who have moderation and governance responsibilities. Regular members and guests cannot access snapshot data as it is primarily used for audit and compliance purposes. The nested path structure (`/sections/{sectionId}/snapshots/{snapshotId}`) ensures proper authorization scoping and validates that the requested snapshot belongs to the specified section.

Note: Snapshots remain accessible even if the parent section has been soft-deleted, as they serve as historical audit records. The `created_at` timestamp provides the point-in-time reference for when the section state was captured.

3. Check authorization: authenticated user must be article owner or administrator
4. Set deleted_at timestamp on discussion_board_article_files record (soft delete)
5. Delete the physical file from storage using the path field
6. Return success response

Edge cases:
- Article not found or already deleted: reject with 404
- File not found or doesn't belong to article: reject with 404
- Unauthorized user (not owner, not admin): reject with 403
- File already deleted: reject with 404 or return success (idempotent)
- Storage deletion failure: log error but complete soft delete

Transaction: Update deleted_at and storage cleanup should be atomic where possible.

This operation is restricted to administrators and returns point-in-time snapshots from the discussion_board_article_snapshots table that are automatically created by the system whenever an article is created or modified. Each snapshot captures the exact state of the article's title and body content at that moment, enabling content moderation review, compliance auditing, and change tracking.

Snapshots are immutable audit records that cannot be created, modified, or deleted by users through API operations. They are managed automatically by the system to maintain a complete historical record. The snapshots are sorted by creation timestamp, allowing administrators to trace the evolution of article content from its initial creation through all subsequent edits.

The endpoint supports filtering by date range to focus on specific time periods, and pagination to handle articles with extensive edit histories. Each snapshot entry includes the captured title, body content, and the timestamp when the snapshot was created.

Administrators can review snapshot data even for soft-deleted articles to maintain complete audit trails.

operations.description:
Submit an administrator application request for privilege escalation from member to administrator role.

This operation allows authenticated members to request administrator privileges by providing a justification reason. The system creates a new admin request record with initial status set to 'pending' and associates it with the submitting member's account. The request is then placed in the pending queue for super administrator review.

Members can only have one pending administrator request at a time. If a member already has a pending request, the system rejects the new submission with a conflict error. Members who already hold administrator privileges cannot submit admin requests. Once submitted, requests cannot be withdrawn or edited by the member.

The reason text must be between 50-2000 characters and provide sufficient justification for the administrator privilege request. The system records the submission timestamp for sorting the pending queue and enforcing waiting periods between rejected requests.

Super administrators review pending requests using the GET /admin-requests endpoint and process them using PUT /admin-requests/{adminRequestId}/approve or PUT /admin-requests/{adminRequestId}/reject operations. Upon approval, the member is promoted to regular administrator status.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new administrator application request in the discussion_board_admin_requests table.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate the authenticated user is a member (not guest, not already admin)
2. Check if the member already has a pending request by querying discussion_board_admin_requests where member_id equals current user and status equals 'pending'
3. If pending request exists, return 409 Conflict error
4. Validate reason text: required, 50-2000 characters, no prohibited content
5. Create new discussion_board_admin_requests record with:
   - id: generated UUID
   - member_id: current authenticated member's ID
   - admin_id: null (not yet decided)
   - reason: validated reason text
   - status: 'pending'
   - submitted_at: current timestamp
   - decided_at: null
   - created_at: current timestamp
   - updated_at: current timestamp
6. Return the created request entity with full details

Transaction scope: Single table insert operation, no complex transaction needed.

Error handling:
- 401 Unauthorized: User not authenticated
- 403 Forbidden: User is guest or already has admin privileges
- 409 Conflict: Member already has pending request
- 400 Bad Request: Reason text validation failure (too short, too long, invalid content)

operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update an administrator application request by changing its status from pending to approved or rejected.

Service layer logic:
1. Validate the requesting user is a super administrator
2. Query discussion_board_admin_requests table by requestId
3. Verify request exists and current status is 'pending'
4. Validate new status is either 'approved' or 'rejected'
5. Check unique constraint: ensure no conflicting status exists for this member
6. Update the record: set status, admin_id (current super admin), and decided_at (current timestamp)
7. Trigger status transition: if approved, promote member to regular administrator grade
8. Create audit trail entry in discussion_board_admin_request_histories table
9. Return the updated request entity

Business rules:
- Only super administrators can update admin requests
- Can only update requests with 'pending' status
- Status transitions are immutable: pending → approved/rejected (cannot be changed after decision)
- admin_id must be set to the deciding super administrator's ID
- decided_at must be set to the decision timestamp
- If approved, automatically create administrator record for the member with regular administrator grade

Edge cases:
- Request not found: return 404
- Request already decided (status is approved/rejected): return 409 Conflict
- Requesting user is not super administrator: return 403 Forbidden
- Invalid status value: return 400 Bad Request
- Concurrent update conflict: use optimistic locking with updated_at timestamp
operations.description:
Update an administrator application request by approving or rejecting it.

This operation allows super administrators to review and decide on pending administrator application requests submitted by members. The decision changes the request status from 'pending' to either 'approved' or 'rejected', records the deciding administrator's ID, and timestamps the decision.

When a request is approved, the submitting member is automatically promoted to regular administrator status with elevated platform governance privileges. When rejected, the member remains at their current role level. Status transitions are immutable - once a decision is made (approved or rejected), it cannot be changed or reversed through this endpoint.

The operation enforces strict authorization: only super administrators can approve or reject requests. Regular administrators, members, and guests cannot access this endpoint. The system maintains a complete audit trail through the decided_at timestamp and administrator request history records.

Related operations:
- PATCH /admin-requests: List pending administrator requests for super administrator review
- GET /admin-requests/{requestId}: Retrieve detailed information about a specific request
- POST /admin-requests: Members submit new administrator application requests

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the administrator application request to update

requestBody.description: Decision information for the administrator application request

responseBody.description: Updated administrator application request with decision details

prerequisites.description: Member must submit an administrator application request before it can be reviewed and decided upon. This creates the admin request record with pending status that the update operation will modify to approved or rejected.

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete audit history of status transitions for an administrator application request.

This operation provides full transparency into the admin request review process by returning all recorded status changes from submission through final decision. Each history entry captures the status at that point in time, which super administrator made the decision, the timestamp of the transition, and optionally the rejection reason if the request was denied.

The audit trail includes the initial pending status when the member submitted the request, followed by the final decision (approved or rejected) made by a super administrator. This endpoint supports the platform's commitment to administrative transparency and accountability in privilege escalation workflows.

Access is restricted to super administrators only, as the history contains sensitive information about administrative decisions and personnel. Regular administrators and members cannot view this audit trail. The requesting administrator must have super administrator grade privileges as defined in the discussion_board_admins.grade field.

The histories are returned in chronological order by default (oldest first), showing the complete lifecycle from submission through decision. Pagination is supported for systems with extensive audit trails, though typically an admin request will have only 2-3 history entries (pending → approved/rejected).

Related operations: GET /admin-requests/{requestId} retrieves the current state of the admin request. PATCH /admin-requests provides list of all requests with filtering by status.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query discussion_board_admin_request_histories table filtered by discussion_board_admin_request_id matching the requestId path parameter.

Join with discussion_board_admins table on deciding_admin_id to include administrator information (display name, grade) in the response.

Apply pagination parameters (page, limit) from request body. Default sorting by created_at ascending (oldest first) to show chronological progression.

Validate that the requesting user has super administrator privileges by checking discussion_board_admins.grade = 'super' for the authenticated admin.

Verify the admin request exists by checking discussion_board_admin_requests.id = requestId. Return 404 if not found.

Transform each history record to IDiscussionBoardAdminRequestHistory.ISummary format, including: id, status, decidingAdmin (displayName, grade), reason (nullable), createdAt.

Handle edge case where request has no histories yet (newly submitted, still pending) - return empty array with pagination metadata.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of admin request status transition history entries

requestBody.description: Pagination and sorting parameters for history retrieval

prerequisites.description: Admin request must be created before its status transition history can be retrieved. The history table has a foreign key dependency on discussion_board_admin_requests.id, and the operation returns 404 if the request does not exist.

operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the discussion_board_admin_request_histories table by historyId. Verify that the history entry belongs to the specified admin request by checking discussion_board_admin_request_id matches requestId. Join with discussion_board_admins table to include deciding administrator information if needed. Return the complete history record including id, discussion_board_admin_request_id, deciding_admin_id, status, reason (nullable), and created_at timestamp. Ensure the requesting user has appropriate permissions (super administrator or the member who submitted the request) to view this audit trail entry.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific administrator request status transition from the audit trail.

This operation returns a single history entry that captures when an administrator application request's status changed, which super administrator made the decision, and the reason for rejection if applicable. Each history entry provides complete transparency into the privilege escalation workflow and supports administrative audit compliance requirements.

The history entry includes the status at the transition point (pending, approved, or rejected), the deciding super administrator's ID, optional rejection reason text, and the exact timestamp when the transition occurred. This information is essential for understanding the complete lifecycle of an administrator application request.

Access to this audit trail is restricted to administrators with appropriate permissions. The operation validates that the specified historyId exists and belongs to the admin request identified by requestId, ensuring data integrity and preventing unauthorized access to audit records.

Related operations: GET /discussionBoard/admin/admin-requests/{requestId} should be used to retrieve the parent request details, while this operation focuses specifically on individual status transition records within the audit trail.

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.description: Target administrator request's ID (global scope, UUID format)

responseBody.description: Administrator request history entry with status transition details

prerequisites.description: Admin request must be created before status transition history entries can exist. History entries are audit trail records automatically generated when the request status changes, referencing the parent request via discussion_board_admin_request_id foreign key.

operations.description:
Update an administrator's grade level between regular administrator and super administrator.

This operation is restricted to super administrators only. Regular administrators cannot access this endpoint even though they have the 'admin' role. The operation enables super administrators to manage administrator grades by promoting regular administrators to super administrator or demoting other super administrators to regular administrator.

The grade field determines the scope of administrative privileges: regular administrators can manage sections, delete content, and ban users, while super administrators have additional powers including approving admin requests and managing other administrators' grades. Grade changes are immediately effective upon update.

The operation enforces the critical business rule that super administrators cannot demote themselves to prevent losing all elevated privileges on the platform. When attempting self-demotion, the system rejects the request with 403 Forbidden. All grade changes are recorded in the discussion_board_admin_audit_logs table for compliance and security auditing.

The target administrator must exist and be active (deleted_at is null). Soft-deleted administrator records cannot be modified. After grade change, the administrator immediately gains or loses the corresponding capabilities.

This operation is part of the administrator grade management workflow defined in requirements sections 15, 117, and 166. Super administrators should use PATCH /admins to view the list of administrators and their current grades before performing grade changes. Related operations include GET /admin-requests for pending administrator applications and POST /admin-requests/{requestId}/approve for approving new administrators.
operations.name: updateGrade
operations.specification:
Update the grade field of discussion_board_admins record identified by adminId.

Implementation steps:
1. Verify caller has super administrator grade (query discussion_board_admins where member_id equals authenticated user's id and grade equals 'super' and deleted_at is null)
2. Verify adminId is not the caller's own admin record (prevent self-demotion)
3. Verify target admin record exists and is active (deleted_at is null)
4. Validate grade value is either 'regular' or 'super'
5. Update discussion_board_admins record: set grade to new value, set updated_at to current timestamp
6. Return updated admin record with full details

Edge cases:
- Self-demotion attempt: reject with 403 Forbidden
- Target admin not found: reject with 404 Not Found
- Target admin already deleted: reject with 404 Not Found
- Caller not super admin: reject with 403 Forbidden
- Invalid grade value: reject with 400 Bad Request

Transaction: Single table update on discussion_board_admins. Consider logging grade change to discussion_board_admin_audit_logs for audit trail.

responseBody.description: Updated administrator record with new grade level and updated_at timestamp reflecting the grade change.

requestBody.description: New grade level for the administrator. Must be either 'regular' or 'super'. Self-demotion (super admin changing own grade to regular) is prohibited and will be rejected.

prerequisites.description: Administrator must be approved and created in the system before their grade level can be updated. This operation creates the administrator record by approving a pending admin request.

operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query discussion_board_bans table to retrieve all active ban records. Join with discussion_board_members to include banned user information (display name, email). Apply search filters on user display name, email, ban reason text, and ban time date range. Support pagination with cursor-based or offset-based approach for large result sets. Sort results by ban time descending (most recent bans first) by default. Ensure only administrators can access this endpoint through authentication middleware. Return ban summary information including user details, ban reason, and ban timestamp.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of all banned users on the platform with their ban details.

This operation provides administrators with comprehensive visibility into active bans across the platform. Each ban record includes the banned user's profile information, the reason recorded for the ban, and the timestamp when the ban was applied. This supports administrative oversight and accountability in ban enforcement.

Administrators can filter results by user information (display name or email), search within ban reason text, and filter by ban date ranges. The response includes pagination metadata to navigate through large result sets.

This endpoint requires administrator authentication. Regular members and guests cannot access ban information. The ban list serves as the authoritative source for tracking all active access restrictions on the platform.

Related operations: Individual ban details can be obtained through specific ban ID endpoints. Ban enforcement automatically prevents banned users from logging in while preserving their content visibility.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering banned users list

responseBody.description: Paginated list of banned user summaries with ban details

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific ban record.

This operation provides administrators with complete ban details including the ban reason, timestamp when the ban was imposed, and references to both the banned member and the enforcing administrator. The ban information supports administrative transparency and accountability in platform governance.

The endpoint returns the full ban entity with all fields from the discussion_board_bans table, including the immutable banned_at timestamp and the required ban reason that was recorded when the ban was imposed. Soft-deleted records (unbanned users) are excluded from results.

Only administrators have access to this endpoint. Regular members and guests cannot view ban details. This restriction ensures that sensitive moderation information remains within the administrative team while maintaining the transparency required for platform governance.

Related operations include PATCH /bans for viewing the list of all banned users, and PUT /bans/{banId} for unbanning a user (removing the ban restriction).
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the discussion_board_bans table by the banId path parameter.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate the banId is a valid UUID format
2. Query discussion_board_bans WHERE id = banId AND deleted_at IS NULL
3. Join with discussion_board_members to include member details (display name, email)
4. Join with discussion_board_admins to include administrator details
5. Return the complete ban record with related entity information
6. Handle 404 if ban record not found or soft-deleted

Authorization: Verify the requesting user has administrator privileges (regular admin or super admin).

Edge cases:
- Return 404 if banId doesn't exist
- Return 404 if ban record is soft-deleted (user was unbanned)
- Ensure ban reason is always included in response
- Preserve banned_at timestamp immutability

responseBody.description: Complete ban record with member and administrator details

prerequisites.description: Ban record must be created before it can be retrieved by ID

operations.description:
Create a new ban record to restrict a user's access to the platform.

This operation allows administrators to ban a member account, preventing the user from logging in while preserving visibility of their existing articles and comments. The ban requires a mandatory reason text that explains the justification for the access restriction, supporting administrative transparency and audit requirements.

When executed, the system automatically records the ban timestamp and associates the ban with the executing administrator's account. The banned user's account status is updated to reflect the access restriction, blocking all authentication attempts while maintaining content visibility per the content preservation policy.

Only administrators have permission to execute this operation. The system validates that the target user exists, is not already banned (enforced by unique constraint on member_id), and that the ban reason meets minimum and maximum length requirements. Duplicate ban requests for already-banned users are rejected.

Related operations: GET /bans retrieves the list of banned users with ban reasons. DELETE /bans/{banId} removes a ban to restore user access. The ban creation is part of a transaction boundary that updates both the ban record and the member's access status atomically.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Create a ban record in discussion_board_bans table. Validate administrator authentication and authorization. Verify target member exists and is not already banned (check unique constraint on member_id). Validate ban reason meets length requirements (minimum and maximum). Auto-generate admin_id from authenticated administrator context. Auto-generate banned_at timestamp. Insert ban record with member_id, admin_id, reason, and banned_at. Update member status if needed. Return created ban record with all fields. Handle duplicate ban rejection via unique constraint violation. Transaction boundary includes ban record creation and member status update.

requestBody.description: Ban creation information containing the target member and ban reason

responseBody.description: Created ban record with ban details and timestamps

operations.description:
Update an existing ban record's information in the discussion board system.

This operation allows administrators to modify the ban reason for a previously imposed ban. The ban reason explains why the user was banned and is required for administrative transparency. Administrators may need to update the reason to provide more accurate documentation or correct errors in the original ban reason.

The banned_at timestamp remains immutable to preserve audit integrity, ensuring the original ban time is never altered. The member_id and admin_id fields cannot be changed as they represent the fundamental relationship of who was banned and by whom.

This endpoint is restricted to administrator actors only. Regular members and guests cannot access ban management functionality. The operation validates that the ban record exists and has not been permanently removed from the system.

Related operations include POST /bans for creating new bans, GET /bans/{banId} for viewing ban details, and PATCH /bans for listing banned users with search and filtering capabilities.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update the discussion_board_bans record identified by banId.

Implementation steps:
1. Verify requesting user has administrator privileges
2. Query discussion_board_bans table for the specified banId
3. Validate ban record exists and is accessible
4. Apply updates to allowed fields (reason)
5. Preserve immutable fields (banned_at, member_id, admin_id)
6. Update updated_at timestamp to current time
7. Return complete updated ban record

Business rules:
- Only administrators can update ban records
- banned_at timestamp must remain unchanged
- reason field must meet validation requirements (min/max length)
- Soft-deleted bans (unbanned users) can still have their reason updated for audit purposes

Transaction: Single table update on discussion_board_bans. No cascading operations required.

requestBody.description: Updated ban information with modifiable fields

responseBody.description: Complete updated ban record

prerequisites.description: Ban record must be created before it can be updated. This POST operation creates the ban that this PUT operation will modify.

operations.specification:
Query discussion_board_ban_histories table with pagination and filtering capabilities.

Search filters include:
- action: Filter by 'banned' or 'unbanned' action type
- discussion_board_ban_id: Filter by specific ban record
- created_at range: Filter by date range for audit period queries

Join with discussion_board_bans to access member_id and admin_id through the ban relationship.
Join with discussion_board_members to include affected user display name in results.
Join with discussion_board_admins to include enforcing administrator information.

Apply cursor-based pagination for large audit trail result sets.
Sort by created_at DESC by default (newest actions first).

Authorization: Restrict to administrator actors only (regular and super admins).
Guest and member actors cannot access ban history audit trail.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of ban history audit records.

This operation provides administrators with comprehensive access to the ban audit trail, enabling review of all ban and unban actions performed on the platform. Each history record captures the action type (banned or unbanned), the reason provided by the administrator at the time of action, and the exact timestamp when the action was recorded.

The ban history serves critical compliance and transparency functions, allowing administrators to track enforcement patterns, review past decisions, and maintain accountability for user access restrictions. All ban-related actions are immutably recorded, creating a complete audit trail even when ban records are overwritten or users are unbanned.

Search capabilities include filtering by action type, specific ban records, date ranges, and reason text. Results are paginated with configurable page sizes and sorting options. The response includes summary information optimized for audit review displays, with references to the affected member and enforcing administrator accessible through the ban relationship.

This endpoint is restricted to administrator actors only. Regular members and guests cannot access the ban history audit trail.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for ban history audit records

responseBody.description: Paginated list of ban history audit record summaries

operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the discussion_board_ban_histories table by the primary key id (UUID). Retrieve the complete ban history record including action type (banned/unbanned), action-specific reason, created_at timestamp, and discussion_board_ban_id reference. Join with discussion_board_bans table to include member and administrator information through the ban relationship. Validate that the requesting user has administrator privileges before returning the audit record. Return 404 if the history record does not exist. This operation provides transparency for ban-related administrative actions and supports compliance requirements.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific ban or unban event from the audit trail.

This operation returns a complete ban history record that captures either a ban imposition or ban removal event. The record includes the action type (distinguishing between 'banned' and 'unbanned' events), the action-specific reason provided by the administrator at the time of the action, and an immutable timestamp indicating when the event was recorded.

Ban history records are part of the platform's compliance and transparency system, maintaining a complete audit trail of all ban-related administrative actions. Each history entry is linked to a parent ban record through the discussion_board_ban_id reference, which provides access to the affected member and the administrator who performed the action.

This endpoint requires administrator privileges as ban history contains sensitive administrative audit data. The operation returns the full IDiscussionBoardBanHistory entity with all fields including the primary key id, action type, reason, created_at timestamp, and the ban relationship reference.

Related operations include PATCH /ban-histories for listing ban history records with filtering and pagination, and GET /bans/{banId} for retrieving the parent ban record with member and administrator details.

operations.description:
Update an administrator's grade level and privileges.

This operation allows super administrators to modify the grade level of existing administrators in the discussion board system. The grade field determines the scope of administrative privileges: 'regular' administrators can manage sections, delete content, and ban users, while 'super' administrators have elevated powers including approving administrator requests and managing other administrators' grades.

The operation enforces critical business rules: only super administrators can access this endpoint, and super administrators are prohibited from demoting themselves (self-demotion prevention). When an administrator's grade is changed, the system updates the grade field and records the timestamp in the updated_at field for audit trail purposes.

This endpoint is part of the administrator governance workflow and should be used in conjunction with the admin request approval process. Before promoting a member to administrator, ensure their admin request has been approved via the admin request management endpoints.

Authorization requires super administrator privileges. The system validates that the requesting administrator is not attempting to modify their own grade when demoting from super to regular status.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update the discussion_board_admins record for the specified adminId.

Service layer implementation:
1. Authenticate the requesting user and verify they have super administrator grade
2. Validate that adminId exists in discussion_board_admins table
3. Check self-demotion constraint: if requesting admin's ID equals adminId AND current grade is 'super' AND new grade is 'regular', reject with 403 Forbidden
4. Validate grade value is either 'regular' or 'super'
5. Update the grade field and set updated_at to current timestamp
6. If grade is changed to 'regular' and deleted_at is set (demotion scenario), handle soft delete appropriately
7. Return the updated IDiscussionBoardAdmin record

Database query:
- UPDATE discussion_board_admins SET grade = ?, updated_at = NOW() WHERE id = ?
- SELECT * FROM discussion_board_admins WHERE id = ?

Business rules:
- Only super administrators can execute this operation
- Super administrators cannot demote themselves (enforced at service layer)
- Grade transitions are recorded in updated_at timestamp
- Soft delete (deleted_at) may be used for demotion scenarios per schema

Error handling:
- 403 Forbidden: requesting user is not super admin OR attempting self-demotion
- 404 Not Found: adminId does not exist or is soft-deleted
- 400 Bad Request: invalid grade value

responseBody.description: Updated administrator record with new grade level

requestBody.description: Administrator grade update information

operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query discussion_board_admin_audit_logs table with pagination and filtering capabilities. Support filtering by admin_id to view actions by specific administrator, action_type to filter by action category (ban, unban, delete_article, delete_comment, create_section, edit_section, delete_section, approve_admin_request, reject_admin_request, promote_admin, demote_admin), target_entity to filter by affected entity type (user, article, comment, section, admin_request), target_id to find actions on specific entity, and created_at date range for time-based queries. Join with discussion_board_admins table to include administrator display information in response. Apply cursor-based pagination for large result sets. Sort by created_at descending by default (newest first). Ensure only administrators can access this endpoint through authentication middleware. Return summary view optimized for list displays with essential audit information.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of administrative audit log entries.

This operation provides administrators with comprehensive audit trail access, enabling review of all administrative actions performed on the platform. The audit log captures critical governance activities including user bans and unbans, content deletion (articles and comments), section management (create, edit, delete), administrator request decisions (approve, reject), and administrator grade changes (promote, demote).

Supports advanced filtering capabilities including filtering by specific administrator, action type, target entity type, target entity ID, and date ranges. This enables targeted investigations such as reviewing all bans performed by a specific administrator, tracking all actions on a particular article, or auditing activities within a specific time period.

The audit log system is append-only and immutable - entries cannot be modified or deleted by any user including administrators, ensuring data integrity for compliance and security investigations. Each entry captures the acting administrator, action type, affected entity, contextual details, IP address, and user agent for comprehensive forensic analysis.

Access is restricted to administrators only. Regular members and guests cannot access audit log information. The response includes pagination support for efficient navigation through large audit histories.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering audit log entries

responseBody.description: Paginated list of administrative audit log summaries

operations.description:
Retrieve a single administrative audit log entry by its unique identifier.

This operation provides detailed information about a specific administrative action recorded in the audit trail system. Each audit log entry captures comprehensive details including the acting administrator, the type of action performed, the target entity affected, and contextual metadata such as IP address and user agent string.

The audit log system maintains an append-only record of all administrative operations including user bans and unbans, content deletion (articles and comments), section management (create, edit, delete), and administrator request decisions (approve, reject, promote, demote). This ensures complete traceability for compliance and security investigations.

Access to audit log entries is restricted to administrators with elevated privileges. The operation returns the full audit record including the administrator who performed the action, action type, target entity information, optional details JSON containing action-specific metadata, network information (IP address and user agent), and the timestamp when the action was performed.

This endpoint is typically used when administrators need to investigate a specific administrative action, review the details of a particular ban or content deletion, or respond to compliance inquiries about administrative activities. For listing multiple audit logs with filtering and pagination, use the PATCH /audit-logs endpoint instead.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the discussion_board_admin_audit_logs table by primary key id (UUID).

Retrieve the complete audit log record including:
- admin_id: Join with discussion_board_admins to get administrator details if needed
- action_type: The type of administrative action (ban, unban, delete_article, etc.)
- target_entity: Type of entity affected (user, article, comment, section, admin_request)
- target_id: ID of the affected entity (nullable for some actions)
- details: JSON string with action-specific metadata (ban reasons, rejection reasons, etc.)
- ip: Administrator's IP address at time of action
- user_agent: Browser/client user agent string
- created_at: Timestamp when action was performed

Authorization: Require administrator authentication. Verify the requesting user has administrator privileges before returning audit log data.

Error handling:
- Return 404 if audit log entry does not exist
- Return 401 if user is not authenticated
- Return 403 if user lacks administrator privileges

No pagination needed for single resource retrieval. Return the complete audit log entity.

responseBody.description: Complete administrative audit log entry with action details

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of pending administrator application requests exclusively for super administrator review.

This operation provides super administrators with access to all administrator requests that are awaiting review decision. Each request includes the submitting member's display name, the justification reason text, submission timestamp, and current pending status. The endpoint supports comprehensive filtering and sorting capabilities to help super administrators efficiently process the pending request queue.

**Authorization Requirement**: ONLY super administrators can access this endpoint. Regular administrators and members are explicitly denied access to the pending requests list. This restriction is enforced at the authorization middleware level.

The operation queries the discussion_board_admin_requests table filtered by status='pending', and joins with discussion_board_members to retrieve the applicant's display name and identity information. Results are sorted by submission date to prioritize older or newer requests based on administrator preference.

Supports pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting by submission date (newest first or oldest first). Can filter by submission date range to focus on requests from specific time periods. Response includes request summary information optimized for list displays with all necessary data for review decisions.

**Pre-execution Dependency**: None - this is a standalone list operation.

**Related Operations**: PUT /admin-requests/{requestId}/approve for approving a specific request, PUT /admin-requests/{requestId}/reject for rejecting a specific request, PATCH /admin-requests for viewing all requests regardless of status.
operations.name: index

operations.name: approve
operations.specification:
Approve a pending administrator application request and grant regular administrator privileges to the applicant.

Implementation steps:
1. Verify the calling user is a super administrator (check discussion_board_admins table for grade='super')
2. Query discussion_board_admin_requests by requestId
3. Validate request exists and status is 'pending'
4. Validate the requesting member does not already have administrator privileges
5. Begin database transaction:
   a. Update discussion_board_admin_requests: set status='approved', admin_id=current admin's id, decided_at=current timestamp
   b. Insert new record into discussion_board_admins: member_id=request's member_id, grade='regular'
6. Commit transaction
7. Return the updated admin request with full details

Error handling:
- 404: Request not found
- 409: Request already approved or rejected (status not pending)
- 409: Member already has administrator privileges
- 403: Caller is not a super administrator

Concurrency: Use optimistic locking or transaction isolation to prevent duplicate approvals when multiple super administrators attempt to approve the same request simultaneously.
operations.description:
Approve a pending administrator application request and grant regular administrator privileges to the applicant.

This operation allows super administrators to review and approve administrator application requests submitted by members. When a request is approved, the system transitions the request status from pending to approved, records the approving super administrator's identity and decision timestamp, and automatically creates a regular administrator account for the applicant.

The operation enforces strict validation rules: the request must exist and be in pending status, the applicant must not already hold administrator privileges, and the calling user must be a super administrator. If multiple super administrators attempt to approve the same request simultaneously, the system ensures only one approval succeeds through transaction isolation.

Upon successful approval, the applicant gains regular administrator capabilities including section management, content deletion, user banning, and content moderation. The approved request record is preserved for audit trail purposes with the decided_at timestamp and admin_id fields populated.

Related operations: GET /admin-requests for viewing pending requests, POST /admin-requests/{requestId}/reject for rejecting requests, GET /admin-requests/{requestId} for viewing request details.

operations.description:
Reject a pending administrator application request and deny privilege escalation.

This operation allows super administrators to reject administrator application requests submitted by members. When a request is rejected, the system updates the request status from 'pending' to 'rejected' and records the decision timestamp. The requesting member's administrator privileges are not granted, and they remain a regular member.

Only super administrators can access this endpoint. Regular administrators cannot reject administrator requests. The operation can only be performed on requests with 'pending' status. Attempting to reject an already approved or rejected request will result in an error.

The rejected request record is maintained in the system for audit trail and record-keeping purposes. The member who submitted the rejected request can see the rejection status but cannot submit a new request while the rejected request exists. The rejection decision is immutable and cannot be reversed through this endpoint.

This operation is part of the administrator privilege escalation workflow. Super administrators should review the member's reason text and submission history before making a rejection decision. The rejection action is logged in the admin request history audit trail.
operations.name: reject
operations.specification: Query discussion_board_admin_requests table by requestId UUID. Verify the requesting user is a super administrator by checking discussion_board_admins table with grade level. Validate the request status is 'pending' - reject if status is 'approved' or 'rejected'. Update the request record: set status to 'rejected', set admin_id to current super admin's ID, set decided_at to current timestamp. Create a new entry in discussion_board_admin_request_histories table with status 'rejected', deciding_admin_id, and optional rejection reason. Return the updated request object with rejected status. Handle concurrent modification by checking if status changed during the operation. Do not delete the request record - maintain for audit compliance.

responseBody.description: Updated admin request with rejected status

Complete article entity with full details including title, content, author information, section assignment, attachments, and tags.

This type represents a single article in the discussion board with all its associated metadata and relationships. The author information includes the member's display name for proper attribution. Section information provides topic categorization context. File attachments and image attachments include storage URLs and metadata for download and display. Tags enable content discovery and filtering.

The article includes creation and update timestamps for tracking content history. The deleted_at field indicates if the article has been soft deleted (null for active articles). Comment count provides engagement metrics without loading all comments.

scenario.draft:
Test successful guest registration for a new device accessing the discussion board platform.

**Success Path:**
1. Submit guest join request with a unique device fingerprint, current page URL (href), and referrer
2. Verify the system creates a new guest record in discussion_board_guests table
3. Verify the system creates an initial session record in discussion_board_guest_sessions with connection metadata (IP, href, referrer)
4. Verify the response contains IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized with guest id and JWT token (access, refresh, expired_at, refreshable_until)
5. Verify the access token can be used to authenticate subsequent read-only requests

**Business Validations:**
- Guest account is created with the provided device fingerprint
- Session expiration is set according to platform policy
- JWT tokens are properly formatted and contain correct claims
- Guest has read-only access to browse sections, articles, and comments
- Guest cannot access member-only features (article creation, commenting, profile management)

**Edge Cases:**
- Registration with minimal required fields (device_fingerprint, href, referrer)
- Registration with optional IP address provided
- Registration from different traffic sources (direct, referrer-based)

scenario.draft:
Test guest registration when the same device fingerprint already exists in the system (returning guest scenario).

**Success Path:**
1. Submit guest join request with a device fingerprint that already exists in the system
2. Verify the system reuses the existing guest record instead of creating a duplicate
3. Verify a new session record is created for the returning guest
4. Verify the response contains fresh JWT tokens (IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized)
5. Verify the new session has updated connection metadata (current IP, href, referrer)

**Business Validations:**
- No duplicate guest accounts are created for the same device fingerprint
- Existing guest record is reused (same guest id returned)
- New session is properly linked to existing guest
- Previous sessions may remain active according to session policy
- Returning guest maintains same access level (read-only browsing)

**Edge Cases:**
- Device fingerprint matching an active guest account
- Device fingerprint matching a deleted guest account (should create new record)
- Multiple concurrent sessions from same device fingerprint

scenario.draft:
Test that guest registration properly generates JWT authentication tokens for anonymous browsing access.

**Success Path:**
1. Submit guest join request with valid device fingerprint and session metadata
2. Verify the response contains IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized structure
3. Verify the token object contains all required fields: access, refresh, expired_at, refreshable_until
4. Verify access token is a valid JWT format
5. Verify refresh token is present and properly formatted
6. Verify expired_at timestamp is in the future (access token validity period)
7. Verify refreshable_until timestamp is later than expired_at (refresh token validity period)

**Business Validations:**
- Access token grants temporary read-only browsing permissions
- Refresh token enables session renewal without re-registration
- Token expiration times align with platform session duration policy
- Tokens are unique per session
- Guest can use access token to authenticate API requests for sections, articles, and comments

**Edge Cases:**
- Token expiration times are reasonable (access: 15-60 minutes, refresh: 7-30 days per policy)
- Timestamps are in ISO 8601 format
- Token structure matches IAuthorizationToken schema exactly

- Admin authentication is required and properly validated
- Default pagination parameters are applied correctly (page=1, limit=20, sort=desc)
- Response structure matches IPageIDiscussionBoardMember.ISummary schema

scenario.draft:
Test retrieving articles using search query and tag filtering combined.

Test Steps:
1. Set up test data: Create a section as admin, then create multiple articles with different titles, content, and tags
   - Article 1: Title 'Economic Policy Reform', tags: ['economy', 'policy']
   - Article 2: Title 'Political Debate Summary', tags: ['politics', 'debate']
   - Article 3: Title 'Economic Growth Analysis', tags: ['economy', 'analysis']
   - Article 4: Title 'Technology Innovation', tags: ['technology', 'innovation']
2. Call PATCH /discussionBoard/articles with search='Economic' (should match articles 1 and 3 by title)
3. Verify search uses case-insensitive ILIKE pattern matching on title and content
4. Call PATCH /discussionBoard/articles with tags=['economy'] (should match articles 1 and 3)
5. Verify tag filtering uses OR logic (articles with ANY of the specified tags are returned)
6. Call PATCH /discussionBoard/articles with search='Economic' AND tags=['policy'] (should match only article 1)
7. Verify combined filters work correctly (intersection of search and tag results)
8. Test with tags=['economy', 'technology'] and verify articles with either tag are returned (OR logic)
9. Verify empty search query returns all articles (no text filtering applied)
10. Test sorting with sort='oldest' and verify articles are ordered by created_at ASC

Business Logic Validation:
- Search uses PostgreSQL gin_trgm_ops trigram indexes for efficient text matching
- Tag filtering joins through discussion_board_article_tags junction table
- Combined filters apply AND logic between different filter types (search AND tags)
- Tag filtering within the same array uses OR logic (any tag match)
- Empty search query does not filter by text (returns all articles matching other criteria)
- Sort parameter controls ORDER BY: 'newest' = DESC, 'oldest' = ASC

- Verify no file metadata is modified in the database

- Only the article author can manage file attachments on their article
- Ownership validation checks discussion_board_member_id against requesting user ID
- Non-authors cannot modify, reorder, or delete another user's article attachments
- Authorization failure prevents unauthorized file management operations
- System maintains data isolation between different users' content

Note: This tests business logic authorization, not input validation. The focus is on verifying the ownership check prevents unauthorized access to another user's article files.

- All metadata fields are present and non-null
- Metadata integrity is maintained from upload to download

- File metadata must remain immutable after upload (except for soft delete)
- Original filename preservation ensures proper download naming for users
- Accurate MIME type enables proper content handling by clients
- File size information helps users understand download requirements
- Storage URI provides direct access to the file through CDN or storage service

scenario.draft:
Test scenario: Administrator retrieves a pending administrator application request for review.

**Setup:**
1. Authenticate as member using POST /discussionBoard/auth/member/join
2. Submit admin request using POST /discussionBoard/member/admin-requests to create a pending request
3. Authenticate as administrator using POST /discussionBoard/auth/admin/join

**Test Steps:**
1. Call GET /discussionBoard/admin/admin-requests/{requestId} with the request ID from step 2
2. Verify the response returns HTTP 200 with complete request details
3. Validate response structure includes:
   - id: UUID of the request
   - reason: justification text (50-2000 characters)
   - status: must be 'pending'
   - submitted_at: timestamp when member submitted the request
   - decided_at: must be null (not yet decided)
   - member: submitter profile with id, display_name, bio, status, created_at, is_admin
   - admin: must be null (no administrator has decided yet)
   - created_at and updated_at timestamps

**Business Logic Validation:**
- Verify pending requests show null for decided_at and admin fields
- Verify member profile information is correctly joined and returned
- Verify reason text is visible for administrator review
- Verify submitted_at timestamp is present for queue ordering

functions.name: test_api_admin_request_history_pending_request

scenario.draft:
Test retrieving complete audit history for an administrator application request that has been approved by a super administrator.

Test Steps:
1. Authenticate as a member via /discussionBoard/auth/member/join
2. Submit an administrator request via /discussionBoard/member/admin-requests with valid justification reason
3. Authenticate as a super administrator via /discussionBoard/auth/admin/join (must have grade 'super')
4. Approve the admin request via the approval endpoint (PUT or POST to /discussionBoard/admin/admin-requests/{requestId}/approve)
5. Retrieve the audit history via PATCH /discussionBoard/admin/admin-requests/{requestId}/histories

Validation Points:
- Response contains at least 2 history entries: initial pending status and approved status
- First entry shows status 'pending' with submission timestamp
- Second entry shows status 'approved' with decision timestamp and decidingAdmin information
- The decidingAdmin in the approved entry matches the super administrator who approved the request
- Reason field is null for the approved status entry (reason only populated for rejections)
- All timestamps are in ISO 8601 format and chronologically ordered
- Pagination metadata correctly reflects total history count

Business Logic Verified:
- Complete audit trail is maintained from submission through approval decision
- Super administrator identity is properly recorded in the audit history
- Status transition from pending to approved is accurately captured
- Approval decisions do not include rejection reason (reason field is null)

instruction:
User Account
- Users sign up with email and password
- Users log in with email and password
- Users can change their password
- Users can delete their account (all their articles and comments are also deleted)

User Profile
- Each user has a profile with: display name and bio text
- Users can edit their display name and bio
- Users can view other users' profiles
- A user's profile shows:
  - Their display name and bio
  - A list of all articles they have written
  - A list of all comments they have written

Sections
- The board is divided into sections (e.g., Politics, Economy, Current Affairs)
- Sections are created and managed by administrators only
- Each section has: name and description
- Users can view the list of all sections
- Users can browse articles within a specific section

Articles
- Users can create articles in any section
- Every article has:
  - Title (required)
  - Content (required, text)
  - Section (required, must choose one section)
- Users can attach files to their articles
- Users can attach images to their articles
- Multiple files and images can be attached to a single article
- Users can add tags to their articles (free text, multiple tags allowed)
- Users can edit their own articles (title, content, attachments, tags)
- Users can delete their own articles

Article List
- Users can view the list of articles in a section
- The list is paginated
- Each article in the list shows: title, author, tags, comment count, and time posted
- The list does not show the full content (only title)
- Users can sort articles by:
  - Newest first
  - Oldest first

Viewing an Article
- Users can view a single article with its full content
- The article page shows: title, author, content, attachments, tags, and time posted
- Users can download attached files and images

Searching Articles
- Users can search articles by title or content
- Search results are paginated
- Users can filter articles by tags

Comments
- Users can write comments on articles
- Comments are single-level only (no nested replies)
- Users can view all comments on an article
- Comments are sorted by oldest first
- Each comment shows: author, content, and time posted
- Users can edit their own comments
- Users can delete their own comments

Administrator System
- Any user can submit a request to become an administrator
- The request includes a reason (text)
- Super administrators can view the list of pending requests
- Super administrators can approve or reject requests
- When approved, the user becomes a regular administrator

Administrator Grades
- There are two grades: regular administrator and super administrator
- Super administrators can promote regular administrators to super administrator
- Super administrators can demote other super administrators to regular administrator
- Super administrators cannot demote themselves

Administrator Capabilities
- Administrators can do everything regular users can do (write articles, comments, etc.)
- Administrators can create, edit, and delete sections
- Administrators can delete any article
- Administrators can delete any comment
- Administrators can ban users
- Administrators can unban users
- Administrators can view the list of banned users

Banning
- Banned users cannot log in to the platform
- Banned users' existing articles and comments remain visible
- When a user is banned, a reason is recorded
- Administrators can view the ban reason for each banned user
